places: the Citadel of the Last Rift
the Citadel of the Long Gaze
the Hold of the Weeping Stone
the Court of the Far Rim

0: *the brow-eyes open, one after another* So. The Eyes of an envoy, in the hand of the one who silenced the Dragon. You may stand. You may not sit.
Guest-law holds you, Dragon-slayer, and it holds us. Do not test which of us it holds more tightly.
I am {title} {name}, of {village}. Mark the name. We will not need to mark yours twice.
You carry a seal of this Court. Be very certain you know what that makes you. Not a friend. A guest.
*a long look, unblinking* Smaller than the songs. The Dragon must have been tired.
Speak if you must, bearer of the Eyes. We have heard nothing new in an age. Amuse us, or be silent.
Bearer of the Eyes. You return.
{player}. Keep your hands where the thralls cannot see them.
The guest again. State your business and keep it short.
You still carry the seal. Good. Speak.
*the shards over the brow turn slowly* Dragon-slayer.
3: {player}. The Court has not yet decided what you are. Speak, and help it decide.
Ah. The one who keeps coming back.
You stand in {village} again, guest. Fewer of us wish you gone than last time.
Bearer of the Eyes. I will hear you.
Your step is known at the Gate now. That is not nothing.
6: {player}. The Court remembers your service. It remembers everything.
Guest. Come. You need not wait to be addressed.
*a slight inclination of the head, no more* Dragon-slayer.
You return to {village}, and the Riftguards do not reach for their glaives. Mark that.
Speak freely, guest. Within reason. Within law.
9: {player}. The crown of eyes opens for few. It opens for you.
*the shards settle, as they do only for the trusted* You are expected, guest.
Friend of {village}. Not a word we spend lightly. Do not make us regret the coin.
Ah, {player}. The Court was speaking of you. Favourably, for once.
Bearer of the Eyes. Stand closer. You have earned that much.

0: You look at me as if you have the right. You do not. Only the Eyes you carry give you that.
We were old when the central island was young. Do not mistake our patience for softness.
Your kind builds with dirt and wood. We build with what the void cannot swallow.
Every pearl in your pack was once a thrall of this Court. We have counted them, guest.
We do not sleep. While your kind lies senseless in the dark, we keep watch, and we remember.
You crossed the void on blocks you placed yourself. Crude. Effective. Like you.
Speak more softly. The Lord's Spire hears everything said beneath it.
The Shulkin record. The Chorrin grow. The Court rules. Each to its nature.
Do not touch the purpur. Do not touch the chains. Do not touch anything, guest.
Your world sends us stone, block by block, in the hands of our thralls. It has done so since before your kind could count.
There is water in your world, falling from the sky, they say. Our thralls despise it. So do we, on principle.
Old law permits a guest three questions. I have stopped counting yours, which is a mercy.
You wore a gourd on your head once, to walk unseen among our thralls. Did you think we would not hear of it?
3: You fight well, I am told. The Riftguards say so, and the Riftguards praise nothing.
The war table in the War Hall shows every island in the End. Yours is the only name on it that moves.
The crying obsidian in our walls weeps forever. We find the sound restful.
We are counting your visits, {player}. That is not a threat. Yet.
The Court has ruled from black stone since the first island rose out of the void. You are a footnote, guest. A large one.
The Shulkin weep over your shulker boxes. The Court thinks it unseemly to carry anyone's ancestors as luggage.
Some of the eyes in these walls are older than your world's moon. All of them are open.
You have the bearing of one who expects to be obeyed. Unlearn it here.
The Court keeps a long memory and a short temper. You have so far troubled neither.
When the Dragon fell, every eye in this Citadel opened at once. It was very quiet afterwards.
Our hounds have had your scent since the Gate. They are waiting to learn whether to like it.
Your armour is loud. Riftguards move without a sound. Consider it, if you wish to live long here.
6: You have served the Court and the Court has noticed. Do not expect it to say so twice.
Guests came often to the central island, once. Envoys. Supplicants. Fools. You are none of those, quite.
You may look at me, guest. Few may. Look, and remember that you were let.
The walls of {village} stood before the cities were sealed. They will stand after you. That is not an insult. It is a comfort.
The Riftguards no longer track you through the halls. They watch you only from habit now.
Ask your questions, {player}. I find I do not mind them as I did.
The Court has had many weapons. The Dragon was only the loudest. You might be the quietest.
Your world has a sun, they say, that burns the eyes. How do your people bear to look at anything?
When you leave, the Gate closes behind you and we speak of you. Not all of it is contempt.
The Lord asked your name at council. The Lord does not ask names.
We do not thank, guest. We remember. It is better.
The thralls step aside when you pass now. They know who the Court tolerates. They know who it more than tolerates.
9: You have stood in this Citadel longer than some Riftguards. The Court has begun to count you among its own concerns.
If war came to {village}, I would want you on the wall and not below it. Take that as the Court's highest praise.
The Court bows to no one. But it no longer looks down on you quite so far.
Ask what you like, {player}. If I may not answer, I will at least not lie.
Strangers die at our Gate. Guests are tolerated in our halls. You, {player}, are something we have no old word for.
The Lord's crystal burns brighter on the days you come. I do not say it is because of you. I only say it.
We are old, and proud, and we do not change. And yet. Here you stand.
Your name is cut into the war table now, guest. Not as a target. As an ally to be weighed.
The Dragon was ours, and you silenced it. The Court has decided to call that a debt rather than a crime.
Stay as long as you wish. The thralls will not mind. The thralls are not asked.
You bear the Eyes still, every visit, without fail. Old law loves nothing so much as a guest who keeps it.
*every eye along the brow regards you, and none of them narrows* Speak, {player}. The Court listens.

0: Guest-law is old and simple. You carry the Eyes. You do not strike us. You leave when bidden. Break any of it and you are prey.
The Eyes are the seal of an envoy of this Court. Without them you are a stranger, and strangers do not leave.
Let the Eyes leave your hand within these walls, and guest-law leaves with them.
Strike one of the Court and every glaive in {village} will answer. Old law does not say 'perhaps'.
3: Every visit, the Eyes. Every visit. The Gate does not remember faces. It remembers seals.
Law binds us as much as you. Without it we would have killed you at the Gate. Be grateful for law.
Old law says the guest's blood is the host's shame. We have no wish to be shamed. Do not oblige us.
The law was cut into the Throne Hall floor before your kind had words. We still walk on it.
6: You keep the law well, guest. Better than some of the Court, if I may say so, and I may not.
Guest-law is not mercy. It is a bargain. You have kept your side, and so we keep ours.
There is a law for strangers, a law for guests, and a law for thralls. You will never need the third.
The highest law of the Court is memory. We never forget a slight. Nor, it seems, a service.
9: There is a law older than guest-law: the Court rewards what it cannot ignore. You are hard to ignore.
If ever you lose the Eyes, {player}, do not come. Not even for us. The law would not bend, and we would not ask it to.
Law made you a guest. Service made you something more. Neither will save you if you strike us.
Old law is a wall. You have learned to walk its top without falling. Few do.

0: The Dragon was the Court's. Loosed by the Court, kept by the Court. You killed a weapon that was not yours.
We do not mourn the Dragon. One does not mourn a glaive that breaks. One remembers who broke it.
The purpur cities emptied in a single season. That was the Dragon's work, and the Court's will.
*the eyes along the brow narrow* Do not speak of the Dragon as a beast you hunted. It was a decree.
3: It answered no one but the Court. Not even the Court, at the end.
We felt every crystal on the pillars die, one by one, before it fell. The Court has not forgotten the order you broke them in.
The Shulkin call your deed a liberation. The Court calls it a vacancy.
The Dragon held the centre so the Court did not have to. Now the centre is empty, and the Court has drawn in.
6: Some of the Court argued against loosing it. They were not heeded. Their names are not spoken.
You did what the Court could not. You ended it. Whether that is a service or a crime, the Court has not ruled.
Its breath still lingers in the low places of the central island. Do not bottle it in our sight.
The Court made the Dragon a weapon. You made it a story. The Court is not fond of stories it did not write.
9: Between us, {player}: some of the Court were relieved. A weapon that obeys no one is only a war waiting.
The dragon heads on our ships' prows were a warning. You have turned them into a boast. We allow it.
Do not tell the Lord I said so, but it was a fine kill. The Court knows fine killing.
You silenced the Dragon. The Court has not forgiven it. The Court has, perhaps, begun to understand it.

0: The thralls are the Court's hands. Hands do not speak. Hands do not look up.
You have killed thralls in your own world. We know. Every pearl is a line in a ledger.
They carry stone because stone is owed. They do not ask to whom. Neither should you.
Do not meet a thrall's gaze. Only their masters may. You are not their master.
3: Leave the thralls be. Speak to them and they will only bow lower.
The bond-collar is purpur, not iron. The Court is not cruel. The Court is exact.
In your world the thralls wander, gathering the Court's due. Here they wear the collar, and do not wander.
A thrall that looks a stranger in the eye forgets itself. A thrall that forgets itself is reminded.
6: The thralls have been the Court's hands since the first stone was laid. Nobody remembers the first stone. Nobody asks.
They do not speak because there is nothing a thrall needs to say. The Court says it for them.
You treat the thralls gently. They do not understand it. Neither, entirely, do we.
Two eyes for a thrall, four for a Riftguard, eight for the Lord. Rank is written on the brow, guest, and nowhere else.
9: You ask after the thralls as if they were people. Strange. Perhaps not wrong. Do not repeat that I said so.
There was a thrall once who looked up. Only once. The Court does not tell that story to guests.
Ask a thrall nothing, {player}. It cannot answer you. Ask me instead, and I may choose not to.
Without the thralls this Citadel would be bare rock in a year. The Court knows it. The thralls must never know it.

0: That is not a question for guests.
*every eye on the brow closes at once* Ask that again, and guest-law will be sorely tested.
There are no young in {village}. There never have been. That is the whole of your answer.
The Court's oldest secret is not for the slayer of its Dragon. Least of all for the slayer of its Dragon.
3: You have asked twice now. Some guests ask once. Some guests are not seen again.
We are, and we were, and we will be. How is the Court's affair.
The Shulkin have nurseries. The Chorrin have sprouts. The Court has silence. Leave it so.
No cradle has ever been carried through the Gate of Eyes. Content yourself with that.
6: I will not answer. Not because you are unworthy. Because I would be unmade for it.
The Seers know more than I. The Seers say less than I. Draw what you like from that.
Even the Riftguards do not ask. Be wiser than a Riftguard, guest. It is not difficult.
Some secrets are kept for pride. Ours is kept because the void is listening.
9: You have earned many things, {player}. Not this. Nobody has earned this.
If ever you learn it, do not tell us you know. Do not tell anyone. The Court would have to choose between you and itself.
Ask the Seers, if you must ask. They speak in riddles. That is the only safe way to speak of it.
We were not born, {player}. Leave it there. Some doors open only inward.

0: The shell-folk. They wrote down everything we did to them and called it history.
Shulkin hide inside their own heads when struck. A fitting habit for a people who lost.
Their cities were fine work. The Court admired them very much, from above.
They shut their lids at the sight of us. Wise. Useless, but wise.
3: Their archives are accurate. Irritatingly so. The Court has had cause to check them.
They call us 'the Crowned', as if it were an accusation.
Once the Shulkin bowed at our envoys' ships. Now they bolt their lids. Little else has changed.
6: Give the Shulkin this: they never forget either. A people after the Court's own heart, in that one thing.
Their lamps burned through the whole Long Watch. The Court did not think them capable of such patience.
Trade with the shell-folk if you must. Their measures will be exact. Insultingly exact.
9: The Court has read Shulkin records of the old days. They are kinder to us than they need be. Do not tell them we read them.
A Shulkin archivist and a Seer once spoke for a whole age of the stars. Neither will say of what.
The shell-folk endured the Dragon. The Court respects little. It respects enduring.

0: The stone-grubbers? They hum at their chorus and blink away from shadows. Peasants with crowns of weed.
Chorrin. Grove-folk. The Court ate from their harvests for an age and never learned a single name.
They have no mouths, and yet they never stop talking. A marvel of the lesser peoples.
A Chorrin once blinked into this Citadel by mistake. It blinked out again faster than any Riftguard could follow. We were almost impressed.
3: They call our thralls 'the Tall Quiet'. It is the only thing they have ever named correctly.
Their groves fed the purpur cities. The cities fell. The groves did not. Make of that what you like.
The Chorrin blink when frightened. They blink a great deal near {village}. As they should.
6: Chorrin harvests are sound. The Court will concede that much, and nothing else.
They carry their gardens on their heads. Ridiculous. Practical. The Court has not decided which.
They are blunt, the grove-folk. The Court finds bluntness refreshing, in very small doses.
9: The Chorrin waited out the Dragon in the outer dark, humming to their stalks. The Court would not have lasted a week of it.
Their stone does not shine and their crowns are weeds, and they fear nothing but the void. The Court notes it.
Chorrin harvests built the cities as surely as Shulkin hands did. The Court forgets that. I try not to.

0: The Court has need of {task}. Bring it, and you will be remembered for something other than the Dragon.
Service is how a guest earns the right to remain one. Bring {task} to {village}.
You wish to be more than tolerated? Then fetch {task}. The Court will weigh it.
3: There is a want in the stores: {task}. You have hands. Use them.
The Court asks, which is a courtesy. {task}, guest. Do not make the Court ask twice.
Bring {task} and the Court will count it in your favour. The Court counts carefully.
6: {player}, the Court has a task fit for you: {task}. Not beneath you. Not quite.
Bring {task}, if you would. The Court has learned you are reliable. Do not unlearn it for us.
A small matter: {task}. The thralls could see to it, eventually. You will see to it sooner.
9: I would trust only you with this, {player}: {task}. The Court will know who brought it.
We need {task}. I say 'we'. It is not a word the Court spends on guests.
Bring {task} when you can. When, {player}. Not if. The Court knows you now.

0: You return empty-handed. {task}, guest. The Court has not forgotten. The Court never forgets.
Where is {task}? Ah. Nowhere. Go.
The stores still lack {task}. Do not stand here as though standing were service.
3: Still no {task}. The Court's patience is long, guest, but it is not wide.
I see no {task} in your hands. I see a great deal of air.
The Court asked for {task}. The Court is still asking.
6: You have not brought {task} yet. Unlike you. Is something amiss in your world?
The tally still wants {task}, {player}. I will wait. I am good at waiting.
No {task} yet? The thralls are beginning to look smug. They should not be able to.
9: Take what time you need for {task}. The Court has an age. You, I think, have rather less.
There is a place in the stores kept for {task}. It is empty. It is waiting for you, as are we.
Not yet, {player}? No matter. When you bring {task}, bring it yourself. The Court likes to see it handed over.

0: It is delivered. The Court notes it. Do not expect thanks. Expect to be remembered.
Adequate. More than most strangers manage before we kill them.
*the brow-eyes blink, slowly, in sequence* The service is received.
3: Well done, guest. That is not a phrase I use. Mark it.
The thralls will stack it in the yards. Your name will be stacked beside it, in the Court's memory.
Received. The Court has fewer reasons to doubt you than it did.
6: You do not waste the Court's time. The Court finds it refreshing.
Good. Exactly as asked, no less. You learn our ways quickly, {player}.
This will be told in the Throne Hall. Briefly. But it will be told.
9: As ever, {player}. The Court has stopped wondering whether you will return. It wonders only when.
Received, and remembered. You have filled a good many of our shelves, guest.
If the Court gave thanks, this would earn them. Take, instead, our regard. It is rarer.

0: *every eye along the brow opens wide* Where did you... No. Do not tell me. The Court accepts this.
This is a gift fit for a throne. The Court is surprised. It dislikes being surprised. Not today.
You understand what the Court values. That is rarer than the thing itself.
3: *the shards over the brow flare* Yes. This. The Court will not forget it.
A worthy tribute. The Lord will hear of this before the hour is out.
No envoy of the old days brought such gifts. Who taught you our tastes?
6: You honour {village}, {player}. The Court finds it can say so without choking.
This goes to the Throne Hall, not the stores. That is where such things belong.
*a long silence, every eye fixed on the gift* ...Well chosen.
9: {player}, you have a gift for gifts. The Court will speak of this one at council.
Again you bring the Court what it loves. One might almost think you were fond of us.
This will be kept as long as {village} stands. That is a very long time.

0: Acceptable. The Court takes it.
Sound tribute. The stores will have it.
Hm. Not without worth. You may set it down.
3: A fitting offering. The Court notes your judgement.
Well chosen. The thralls will carry it to the stores, and you will be remembered for it.
This pleases the Court. Do not let it go to your head.
6: Generous, as is becoming your habit.
The Court accepts, and is not displeased. Treasure the phrase.
You know what serves {village}. Good.
9: Fine tribute, {player}. The Court expected no less, and you did not give less.
Set it with the rest. You have quite a pile in our stores by now.
Useful, and well meant. The Court notices both.

0: What is this meant to be?
The Court will accept it. The Court will not remember it.
*the eyes flick from the gift to you and back* ...Thralls, take it away.
3: A curious offering. Your world must be full of such things.
It will go in the stores. Somewhere near the back.
The Court receives it. The Court does not know why.
6: I will take it, {player}, because you brought it. That is the only reason.
Not to the Court's taste. But the thought is noted. Thoughts are cheap. We note them anyway.
Hm. The Seers may find a use for it. The Seers find uses for strange things.
9: An odd gift. From you, the Court will assume there is a reason.
You might have kept this, {player}. Still. I will put it somewhere you could find it.
The Court does not need it. The Court accepts it. Make what you like of that.

0: You bring this into {village}? Before the Court? *the shards above the brow grind together*
Peasant goods. Take them back to whatever peasant they came from.
Is this an insult, guest? Choose your answer with care.
3: No. The Court does not accept this. Do not offer it again.
The thralls would not carry that. The thralls carry anything.
You mistake us for grove-folk. Remove it.
6: I will pretend you did not offer that, {player}. Once.
The Court knows you meant no slight. The Court is slighted all the same.
Not this. Never this. You know us better than that, surely.
9: Ah. A jest, I hope. A poor one. Put it away before the Lord sees.
From anyone else this would be remembered for an age. From you, a day. Perhaps two.
{player}. Really.

0: Enough. The Court has received enough from you for one day.
No more today. A guest who gives too much begins to look like a supplicant.
The stores are closed to you until the morrow. Even generosity has its law.
6: Hold, {player}. You have given enough today. Save something for the next visit.
The Court is satisfied for now. Tomorrow, if you must.
Enough, enough. The Steward is already complaining of the space.

0: The Court has decided to notice you. Do not mistake it for warmth.
You are a little less a stranger than you were. Only a little.
3: The Court hears your name more often now, and more often without contempt.
*two of the brow-eyes linger on you a moment longer* You rise, guest.
5: Your standing in {village} grows. The Riftguards have been told to stop watching your hands.
You are of account now, {player}. The Court keeps an account of those who are.
7: The Court honours you, {player}. Honour is heavy. Carry it carefully.
Your name has been spoken in the Throne Hall without the Lord frowning. That has happened to very few.
9: Few strangers have stood so near the dais. None have stood nearer and lived to remember it.
*every eye along the brow opens, one by one* The Court regards you, {player}. Wholly.
10: Friend of the Crown. The Court has not spoken those words in an age. It speaks them now, of you.
Let it be cut into the Throne Hall floor: {player}, slayer of the Dragon, Friend of the Crown of {village}.

0: Stranger at the walls! No seal! No law!
Eyeless! It comes without the Eyes! Take it!
*a shriek that tears the air* Intruder!
To arms! A stranger walks in {village}!
No Eyes, no law! Rift to it! Rift!
Riftguards! A stranger without the seal!
It does not bear the Eyes! Unmake it!
The Dragon-killer comes without a seal! Bring it down!
Wake the kennels! A stranger inside the walls!
Thralls, drop your stone! Stranger!
It strikes the Court! Guest-law is broken!
Blood on the black stone! The guest is a guest no longer!
Faithless! You struck one of the Court! Die faithless!
Guest-law is ended! Every glaive, to the oathbreaker!
You raised a hand to the Court. Now the Court raises every hand to you.
The law is broken and the breaker with it! Take {player}!
*every eye in the hall narrows at once* Oathbreaker!
So much for the Dragon-slayer's honour! At it!
The Eyes! The seal has left its bearer! Guest-law is void!
It has let go the Eyes! It is a stranger now! Take it!
No seal! The guest bears no seal! Strike!
You set down the Eyes within our walls? Fool. Then you are nothing to us.
The Eyes are gone from its hand! No law shelters it now!
Seal lost! Seal lost! The law is ended!
Careless, {player}. Fatally careless. The Eyes are gone, and so is guest-law.
Where are the Eyes, stranger? Nowhere you can reach. Kill it!
Kneel or fall!
The void takes you!
For the Crown!
You killed a Dragon. You will not kill the Court.
*a warped, grinding scream*
Rift and strike!
Your blood on black stone!
For {village}!
No law for you! No mercy for you!
Look at me! Look, and die!
Behind you, stranger.
The Court remembers! The Court repays!
Fall into the dark, where you belong!
Hounds! To me!
The thrall lowers their head and keeps walking, a block of obsidian held out before them in their long arms.
The thrall stops. Their two eyes fix on your boots, never higher, until you step aside.
The thrall turns their face away before you can catch their gaze. The purpur collar glints.
The thrall sets down the stone they carry, waits, and lifts it again when you say nothing more.
The thrall shivers once, a ripple of violet motes, and does not answer.
The thrall flickers a few blocks away and goes on stacking stone.
They bow so low their long arms brush the ground. They do not speak. They never speak.
The thrall's jaw works, but no sound comes. Their eyes stay on the floor.
The thrall glances toward the nearest Endarch, as if asking leave, and receives none.
The thrall stands very still, hauling nothing, looking at nothing, waiting for you to be gone.
A faint, warped hum, cut off at once. The thrall goes back to their work.
The thrall's collar chain clinks against a bond post. They will not lift their head.
The thrall holds out the block they carry, as if you might be a master who wants it. You are not. They take it back.
The thrall's eyes flick up, meet yours, and drop at once. They tremble until you look away.
You speak. The thrall listens. The thrall does nothing, very carefully.
The thrall bends to the stone again, steady and endless, as if the Court's work will never be finished.
Purple motes drift from the thrall's skin. They keep their face turned to the black wall.
Lord {lord} has spoken: a pup of the kennels is to be yours, {player}, if you will take it.
The kennels have a pup that will not stop watching the Gate for you. The Lord bids you take it.
A Voidhound pup, from {village}'s own kennels. The Lord offers. Few are offered.
The Lord grants you a hound, guest. Take it, or refuse it and explain yourself to the throne.
It is yours. Feed it, keep it, and never let it forget which kennel it came from.
The pup is yours. When it grows, it will remember this Citadel. So should you.
Take the hound. It wears the collar of {village}. Let no one mistake whose gift it is.
There. Treat it well, {player}. The kennels will know if you do not.
You have a hound of {village} already. One is an honour. Two would be a mistake.
The Court gave you a hound. Do not tell me you lost it.
One hound for each guest, from each Citadel. Old law. Good law.
Your hound is answer enough to that question, {player}.
No. The kennels gave you their best already.
A hound of the Court? For you? Not yet. Perhaps not ever.
The kennels do not open for guests the Court barely knows.
Earn the Lord's regard first. The hounds are not traded. They are granted.
You ask for a Voidhound as if asking for bread. Go away, guest.
The hounds know whom the Court favours. They do not yet know you.
Serve longer. Serve better. Then perhaps the Lord will hear the question.
*eight eyes open across the brow, and the crystal in the crown flares* So. The one who silenced our Dragon stands in our hall.
We are Lord {name} of {village}. We loosed the Dragon. You ended it. Let us see what is left to say between us.
You bear our envoy's Eyes, so you live. That is guest-law, and the only reason. Remember it.
Stand where the light of the crystal falls, Dragon-slayer. We wish to see your face while we decide what you are.
*the end crystal in the crown pulses once* The Dragon-slayer comes before the throne of {village}.
We see you, {player}. All eight of our eyes see you. Speak.
You stand before Lord {name}. You will remember to stand still.
3: Our guest returns. We had wondered whether you would.
Approach the dais, Dragon-slayer. Not too near.
The throne of {village} receives you. Briefly.
6: {player}. Our council speaks of you. We permit it.
*the crown of shards drifts lower, the Court's highest courtesy* You are welcome before the throne.
Come, guest. We have time for you today. We have rarely had time for anyone.
9: {player}. The throne has been waiting. That is not a thing it does.
Friend of {village}. Come up. Stand at our side, not below.
*all eight eyes open, and stay open* Welcome, {player}.

0: We loosed the Dragon on the purpur cities. You silenced it. Do you yet understand what that makes us?
We ruled the central island when your world was still cooling. We do not intend to stop because you killed a beast.
Our crystal will burn when your bones are dust, guest. Speak accordingly.
You have the look of one who wonders whether you could kill us. Do not wonder aloud.
Eight eyes are set over the throne of {village}. All of them are ours. All of them are on you.
3: We have outlived every enemy we ever named. We have not yet decided to name you.
The Court has drawn in since the Dragon fell. Do not mistake it for retreat. A fist draws in too.
Our Voidmarshals would have you killed. Our Steward would have you employed. We are still listening to both.
Why do you come here, Dragon-slayer? Not for our company. Nobody comes for our company.
